text:
Youth daily activity and weekly activity mix

CDC's general recommendation for children and adolescents aged 6–17 is at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity each day. Most should be aerobic, with vigorous aerobic activity on at least three days each week. Muscle- and bone-strengthening activity are each included on at least three days weekly as part of the daily activity, rather than as separate additional sixty-minute blocks. Choices should be varied, age-appropriate and enjoyable.

Population-level activity guidance for ages 6–17. The daily amount covers the activity mix; the weekly components do not require separate additional sixty-minute sessions. This is not an individualized basketball workload or an adopted project planning threshold.
title: Youth daily activity and weekly activity mix

reference_text: For children and adolescents aged 6–17, CDC describes the talk test as a general way to interpret activity intensity: moderate effort permits talking but not singing, while vigorous effort permits only a few words before a pause for breath. It notes that bicycling or basketball may occur at either intensity, so a sport's name alone does not determine the effort. Activities should be enjoyable, safe and appropriate for age and skill.
required_context: A general intensity description within youth physical-activity guidance, not a clinical test, a numeric heart-rate cutoff or a universal classification of every basketball session. It does not establish individual readiness or planner eligibility.

reference_text: CDC encourages enjoyable physical activity, including structured and unstructured forms, family routines, access to equipment and places to be active, and positive encouragement. Activities should fit the child's age. Its safety discussion gives helmets or pads for activities such as cycling, scooter riding, skating and rock-wall climbing as examples of protective equipment. Those examples are activity-specific, not a statement that every sport uses the same equipment.
